It is important to maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and Medical Tests: While using this medication, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as complete blood counts, liver function tests, skin examinations, and Pap smears, should be conducted. Missed Dose: It is crucial to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Storage: Refer to the product instructions and consult your pharmacist for proper storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. Medical Alert: Your condition may lead to complications during a medical emergency. Uses: This medication is used to treat certain types of arthritis (rheumatoid arthritis, arthritis of the spine, psoriatic arthritis), specific bowel diseases (Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis), and a severe skin condition (chronic plaque psoriasis). These conditions involve the immune system attacking healthy tissues. Infliximab works by blocking the activity of a natural substance in the body called tumor necrosis factor-alpha. How to Use: Read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist before starting infliximab and each time you receive a refill. This medication is administered via injection into a vein over at least two hours, as directed by your doctor. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, weight, and response to treatment. Infusion reactions may occur during the administration of this drug. Your doctor may prescribe additional medications before each treatment to help prevent these side effects. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of infusion reactions, such as pain or swelling at the injection site, shortness of breath, flushing, chills, fever, or headache. Do not shake the medication. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration; do not use the liquid if either is present. Use this medication regularly to achieve the most benefit. Side Effects: Common side effects may include headache, stomach pain, or nausea. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. Rarely, this drug may cause serious, potentially fatal liver disease. Heart problems, such as heart attacks, may occur during the infusion and up to 24 hours afterward. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before using infliximab, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other infliximab products, or any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other issues. Infliximab may increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections. Avoid contact with individuals who have infections that can spread easily (e.g., chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, flu). Inform your healthcare professional that you are using infliximab before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor.
